page: Amazon Web Services t2.large is a burstable general purpose instance powered by the Xen hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 burstable vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 45 MB of L3 cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, alongside instruction set support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA.

The hardware configuration excludes integrated local disk storage and dedicated GPU hardware, requiring workloads to rely exclusively on remote Elastic Block Store volumes. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Due to its burstable CPU allocation model and older processor generation, raw compute and memory throughput metrics rank predominantly in the bottom quartile across standard industry tests. Synthetic benchmarks record a Geekbench single-core score of 876.0 and multi-core score of 1571.0, while PassMark registers a CPU score of 2372.18 and a memory score of 950.63. Large-block memory read bandwidth caps at 20.07 GB/sec, and static web serving achieves 2.08 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance targets intermittent workloads that operate below their baseline CPU entitlement for extended intervals and accumulate burst credits. Sustained, compute-intensive execution exhaust available credits and degrade processing velocity. The server functions effectively for non-production environments, moderate traffic web servers, staging databases, lightweight background workers, and development testing suites that require an 8.0 GB RAM footprint without requiring sustained high CPU throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services t2.large is a burstable general purpose cloud instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs and 2 physical cores backed by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, matched with 8.0 GB of memory and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, depending fully on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing reflects its legacy architecture and burstable throttling model, placing CPU and memory throughput in the lower percentiles, such as a PassMark CPU score of 2372.18 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1571.0. The configuration provides economical resource density for workloads with fluctuating or low average CPU utilization, including development environments, lightweight background tasks, staging servers, and low-traffic web applications.
